title: Phishing & Social Engineering Policy Template
metaDescription: Protect your organization with our comprehensive phishing and social engineering policy template. Includes prevention strategies and response procedures.
description: A comprehensive policy template to help organizations establish clear guidelines for recognizing, preventing, and responding to phishing attacks and social engineering tactics. Includes employee training requirements and incident response procedures.

sections.heading: Policy Overview and Purpose
sections.content: This policy establishes guidelines to protect {{ORGANIZATION_NAME}} from phishing attacks and social engineering tactics. Our goal is to educate employees on recognizing threats, implementing protective measures, and responding appropriately to suspicious activities. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties with access to our systems and information.

sections.heading: Definitions and Common Threats
sections.content: Phishing: Fraudulent attempts to obtain sensitive information by impersonating trusted entities through email, text, or phone calls. Social Engineering: Psychological manipulation tactics used to trick individuals into divulging confidential information or performing actions that compromise security. Common threats include: spear phishing (targeted attacks), business email compromise, vishing (voice phishing), smishing (SMS phishing), and pretexting scenarios.

sections.heading: Employee Responsibilities
sections.content: All employees must: verify sender identity before responding to requests for sensitive information, hover over links to check destinations before clicking, report suspicious emails to {{IT_CONTACT}}, never provide passwords or credentials via email or phone, use secure browsers like Incognito Browser for sensitive activities, and attend mandatory security awareness training sessions annually.

sections.heading: Email Security Guidelines
sections.content: Exercise caution with: urgent requests for financial information, emails with generic greetings or poor grammar, unexpected attachments or links, requests to update account information, and communications claiming to be from executives requesting unusual actions. Always verify requests through separate communication channels when in doubt.

sections.heading: Incident Response Procedures
sections.content: If you suspect a phishing attempt: do not click links or download attachments, forward the suspicious email to {{SECURITY_EMAIL}}, change passwords if credentials may have been compromised, immediately report any successful attacks to {{IT_CONTACT}}, and document the incident including time, sender information, and actions taken.

sections.heading: Technical Safeguards
sections.content: {{ORGANIZATION_NAME}} implements: email filtering and spam detection systems, multi-factor authentication for all accounts, regular security updates and patches, employee access controls and permissions reviews, secure browsing tools and VPN requirements, and network monitoring for suspicious activities.

sections.heading: Training and Awareness
sections.content: All employees receive: initial security awareness training within {{TRAINING_TIMEFRAME}} of employment, annual refresher training sessions, simulated phishing tests to assess awareness levels, updates on emerging threats and attack methods, and access to security resources and reporting channels.

sections.heading: Policy Violations and Consequences
sections.content: Violations of this policy may result in: mandatory additional training, restricted system access, formal disciplinary action up to and including termination, and potential legal action in cases of intentional misconduct. The severity of consequences depends on the nature and impact of the violation.

useCases: Small businesses establishing their first cybersecurity policies
HR departments creating employee security guidelines
Educational institutions protecting student and staff data
